correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the bounded heat-conjugated multiplier for s>t and the dense-range factorization. Continuity identifies surface-operator positivity with all finite Gram inequalities by atomic approximation in one direction and local smooth approximation to atoms in the other. For s≤t the upward link into a high zonal test degree gives an unbounded ratio of the subtracted to the positive diagonal. In each |m|>0 block the compact maximizer, replaced by its modulus and extended by zero, has strictly smaller image norm than under the zonal links, where at least one coordinate increases strictly. The two zonal column-parity products are irreducible compact nonnegative Jacobi matrices; the nonnegative top vector is strictly positive and equality in the modulus comparison forces any maximizing vector to have its sign, yielding simplicity. Local norm analyticity and the certified opposite signs give isolated ties and at least two reversals. Independently rebuilt the rational 16-column tests: all three upper tests have eight positive pivots, the first lower minor is −48529856/120670225, the two other lower witnesses are 29/15 and 4/3, and the squared tail error is <10^−18. The critical null equation makes an atomic annihilator Gaussian-decaying and thus smooth, impossible for a nonzero atomic measure. Conversely a normalized top left singular vector, iterated through the Gaussian-decaying finite-band CC*, decays faster than any fixed Gaussian and yields a nonzero smooth annihilating density on undoing the half-heat, with nullity one or two as stated. Subcritical coercivity on heat-smoothed measures gives uniform density by duality.
residual_risks: The comparisons guarantee at least two isolated switches, not a complete classification of all ties or extensions to other multipliers.
